- If sentiment is positive (≥0.5) and forecast is below true outcome, increase forecast by 1–2% to capture bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.5) and forecast is above true outcome, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overreaction.  
- After a sharp price spike (true > forecast by >5%), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 3–5% in next 3–5 days to avoid overshoot.  
- If recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model often underestimates rebound; add 1–3% to forecast for next 2–4 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is consistently 2–3% below true outcome over 3+ consecutive days, apply a 2–4% upward bias to correct for lagged trend.  
- If sentiment history shows no clear direction (all 0.00), model tends to be overly conservative; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid underestimating volatility.
